Whichever actor draws WM_ROSTER_BRET runs the real wm_arcade_move_bret control layer every tick with a real visual backend (wm/bret_backend.h) and real movement (wm/movement.h): convert_facing, set_velocities, execute_walk's dispatch, and change_walk_anim's leg-cycle reselection (all 12 hrt_walkM_fF_anim sequences) are all translated, so a Bret actor with real input genuinely walks with the correct animation. FACING_DIR/NEW_FACING_DIR tracking is now fully real, not substituted: wm/arcade/wm_arcade_closest.h's wm_arcade_update_newfacing translates WRESTLE.ASM:3018's update_newfacing (live NEW_FACING_DIR toward the opponent, every tick, for every actor -- wired into wm_match_tick unconditionally, matching WRESTLE.ASM's own main-loop placement), and wm/movement.h's wm_execute_walk translates set_rotate_anim's literal FACING_DIR=NEW_FACING_DIR catch-up for the #zip/stance case (WRESTLE.ASM:5082-5083) -- exactly like the source, FACING_DIR stays frozen at its last idle value while actually walking, since change_walk_anim's leg half never writes it. Both actors' initial position AND facing now come from the same real WRESTLE.ASM:2691-2755 #set0 wrestler-placement init: wm/match.h's place_wrestler sets x_int/z_int/x_fixed/z_fixed and facing_dir/new_facing_dir together from the real #teamX_starts table (RING_X_CENTER-85,1127+93,WM_MOVE_UP_RIGHT for P1; RING_X_CENTER+85,1103+93,WM_MOVE_DOWN_LEFT for the opponent -- the only reachable first-player-on-team row, RING_X_CENTER=0x400+50 from RING.EQU) instead of a zeroed default; verified these two positions are chosen so each wrestler's real starting facing already points at the other's real starting position (wm_arcade_update_newfacing recomputes the identical value), so nothing spuriously turns on the very first tick. change_walk_anim's leg and torso reselection now also honors execute_walk's own top-of-function INTURN freeze (WRESTLE.ASM:5222-5252, 'treat it like UNINT'): movement and reselection are held while a turn animation (leg or torso) is still playing, load-bearing for correctness since without it the instant FACING_DIR catch-up would truncate every turn to a single tick. set_rotate_anim's own turn-animation *selection* for the #zip/idle-turn case is now wired too (wm_bret_rotate_anim, hrt_rotate_anims_table, BRET.ASM:2871, its 12 real hrt_N_to_M_turn_anim off-diagonal sequences transcribed from HRTSEQ1.ASM including its real reverse-rotation SUBR aliasing), so idle facing changes genuinely animate a turn now, not just update state silently. change_walk_anim's torso half (hrt_torso_anims_table, BRET.ASM:2981) is now fully wired too, diagonal and all 12 off-diagonal entries: the diagonal (FACING_DIR and NEW_FACING_DIR in the same compass quadrant, i.e. not mid-turn) resolves to hrt_torso2_anim/hrt_torso4_anim (hrt_torso8_anim/hrt_torso6_anim are themselves SUBR aliases of those two in HRTSEQ1.ASM, not distinct artwork, confirmed by extracting and comparing their frame data), and the off-diagonal entries resolve to their real hrt_N_to_M_turn2_anim sequence. Each of those 12 carries one or two real ANI_SETFACING commands (HRTSEQ1.ASM:460-524) -- ANIM.ASM's own unconditional, live FACING_DIR=NEW_FACING_DIR copy -- hand-traced to the exact frame index they fire at and fired there by wm_bret_backend_tick, which is what actually promotes FACING_DIR toward NEW_FACING_DIR while genuinely walking (as opposed to the #zip case's instant copy). Translating this also surfaced and fixed a real pre-existing gap: Bret's 6 wired attack animations lead with a real ANI_SETMODE,MODE_UNINT|MODE_NOAUTOFLIP (HRTSEQ2.ASM) that this port's simplified change_anim callback never propagated onto actor->anim_mode, so an attack's own visual sequence was silently reselectable by execute_walk's own dispatch on the same tick once the new idle-turn selection above went live; wm_bret_backend_change_anim now sets that bit for the 6 attack ids (mirroring the same 'ANI_SETMODE is a zero-tick instant command' reasoning already used for MODE_INTURN) and wm_bret_backend_tick clears it back to MODE_NORMAL when the attack naturally ends, matching HRTSEQ2.ASM's own trailing ANI_SETMODE,MODE_NORMAL. Its idle stance and 6 light/power punch/kick animations resolve to real wm_visual_sequence data, and each of those 6 now fires ANIM.ASM's real ATTACK_ON/ATTACK_ON_Z/ATTACK_OFF (wm_arcade_ani_attack_on(_z/_off), real since fix38) at the exact frame index hand-traced from each attack's own HRTSEQ2.ASM source, setting real attack_mode/attack_xoff/.../WM_MODE_CHECKHIT. wm_match_tick now also calls the real, ctest-verified-since-fix38 wm_arcade_check_wrestler_collisions()/wm_arcade_wrestler_hit() (REACT1.ASM) every tick through wm_arcade_wrestler_hit_collision_callback, and wm_bret_backend_tick sets a real per-frame victim hurt_box (wm_arcade_set_hurt_box) via wm_bret_hurt_box_for_frame: the original ANI3 hit-box header (SYS.EQU IANI3X/Y/Z/ID) is confirmed unrecoverable (its bretimg.tbl/bret.seq/imgtbl.glo compile output is absent from the checked-in tree, and the WIMP .IMG directory format doesn't carry it either), so this substitutes each frame's own real WIMP image bounds (width/height/xani/yani, via the new geometry-only src/generated/bret_frame_geometry.c -- deliberately separate from wm_bret_sprite_find's pixel data so hit-box math doesn't depend on which artwork happens to be linked in) as the hurt box. A wired attack whose real attack box overlaps that derived hurt box now actually registers a hit and calls the real, shared wm_arcade_adjust_health (wm/arcade/wm_arcade_lifebar.h, LIFEBAR.ASM:1547-1670): life clamped to [0,LIFE_MAX], the 20+pt near-death 'fudge', 'attract mode never dies', and -- once life genuinely reaches 0 -- a real WM_PMODE_DEAD transition (SETMODE DEAD + wres_collis_off) or, when the attacker has an active combo, LIFEBAR.ASM's own 1-HP combo-revival deferral (I_WILL_DIE, currently unreachable since nothing sets combo_count yet). The same function backs BRET.ASM mode_normal's own I_WILL_DIE self-death resolution (wm_bret_backend_callbacks now wires adjust_health for real instead of leaving it NULL). wm_arcade_adjust_health also now translates LIFEBAR.ASM:1429-1466's own damage-shaping step, applied to delta before the range check: an attacker with an active COMBO_COUNT entirely replaces the hit's damage with -max(10-COMBO_COUNT,4) (currently unreachable, same as the combo-revival case above), and otherwise a nonzero DAM_MULT scales it by (1+DAM_MULT)/2 and is cleared -- so wm_arcade_wrestler_hit's own real, already-ctest-verified-since-fix38 DAM_MULT=2 first-hit-of-the-round bonus and DAM_MULT=4 high-risk bonus (both previously computed and then silently discarded, since nothing ever consumed runtime->dam_mult) now genuinely inflate damage. wm_arcade_adjust_health also now applies LIFEBAR.ASM:1471-1521's own damage_mod_table scaling to any negative (damage, never healing) delta -- WM_ARCADE_DAMAGE_MOD_85PCT (218/256): the real table scales by active-drone-count and drone-vs-player target, but wm_match's actors[] is always the fixed pair wm_match_start_attract/selected create, so that count is always 0 and both of the table's 0-drones columns are the identical _85PCT anyway. wm_arcade_adjust_health also now applies LIFEBAR.ASM:1524-1528's speed_adjustment scaling, unconditionally (healing and damage alike): delta=(delta*WM_ARCADE_SPEED_ADJUSTMENT_16_16)>>16. This port has no live operator-settings/CMOS system to read a real ADJSPEED (1-5) from, so rather than inventing a value, it uses the arcade's own factory-shipped default: AUDIT.ASM's FACTORY_TABLE lists ADJSPEED (adjustment id 25) as 3, exactly matching LIFEBAR.ASM:161's own BADCHK fallback for an out-of-range read, and LIFEBAR.ASM's #timer_table[3-1] entry (0x10000*1) is literally commented 'normal damage (default)' -- i.e. the real factory default is precisely a 1.0x identity multiply, so this line has no effect today but is real and wired for a live value once this port has a settings system. Everything past SETMODE DEAD (death sound, wrestler-type death-animation dispatch, royal-rumble/8-on-1 bookkeeping) is also not translated -- a dead actor's player_mode changes but nothing renders it. wm_arcade_adjust_health now also stamps victim->last_damage with the real pcnt on every call (LIFEBAR.ASM:1593-1595), unconditionally regardless of which branch above ran -- REACT1.ASM's wm_arcade_wrestler_hit already read last_damage for its reduced_damage rapid-hit window (elapsed_word(pcnt,last_damage)<=50 -> WM_RD_* instead of WM_D_*) but nothing had ever written it, so repeated attacks always dealt full damage regardless of timing; a second hit on the same victim within 50 ticks now genuinely deals less. wm_match_tick also now steps wm/arcade/wm_arcade_round.h's wm_arcade_round_tick every tick: WRESTLE2.ASM::match_timer's real get_live_bits() check plus its 5-second (WM_ARCADE_PIN_TIMEOUT_TICKS = 5*TSEC) pin-idiot-check countdown -- the actual source trigger for a round ending on a knockout, not just its round clock running out. Once one PLYR_SIDE has no live wrestler, the countdown starts for real; when it elapses, wm_match_state.round_state.decided/decided_winner_side become real (a simultaneous double-KO resolves as a draw, decided_winner_side=-1, rather than guessing at the unported PIN system's real tie-break). wm_match_tick now also awards the real LIFEBAR.ASM::set_winner round on the exact tick round_state.decided flips false-to-true: wm_arcade_match_score_t tracks real best-of-3 p1rounds/p2rounds and sets match_winner (1 or 2) once either side reaches 2, matching set_winner's KO branch (LIFEBAR.ASM:5070-5147) specialized to this port's fixed 1-on-1 match, where the source's own DID_PIN-priority search among multiple survivors is moot (at most one wrestler per side ever exists here). A simultaneous double-KO (decided_winner_side=-1) awards nothing, matching how the source's own equivalent 'found nobody alive' case is explicitly flagged as should-never-happen rather than a normal path. Not translated: set_winner's #tmout branch (LIFEBAR.ASM:5149+, awarding by average team life when the round clock -- which this port doesn't have -- expires instead of a KO), match_timer's own CREATE PINHIM_ANIM_PID pin-prompt process and the buckoff/reversal window announce_rnd_winner grants afterward, 8-on-1/8-on-2 team bookkeeping and crowd-wake (no team system exists here), match_time's on-screen countdown display and its ADJSPEED-based decrement rate, and everything once a round is actually awarded beyond the score itself (DO_ROUNDS' round-2 restart, match_over, postgame_audits, and the announcer) -- wm_match_tick keeps ticking exactly as before even after match_winner becomes nonzero. This connects for real once an attacker plays a wired attack animation. wm/arcade/wm_arcade_closest.h now translates WRESTLE.ASM's calc_closest delta/distance computation (closest_xdist/closest_ydist/closest_zdist/closest_dist against actor->smart_target) and wm_match_tick calls it every tick before wm_arcade_move_bret, so BRET.ASM's do_punch (near(a,50,45)) sees real distances instead of the permanent 0/0 that used to make every punch resolve to the unwired WM_BRET_ANIM_BUTT2/4 headbutt: a human punching from realistic (non-point-blank) range now gets a real, wired punch animation through ordinary play. calc_closest's own multi-candidate ranking loop (biased_range, ONGROUND/WHOIHIT/INRING/previous-closest/combo/Z-distance biasing, the running-behind-us skip rule, CLOSEST_NUM selection itself) is not translated, since it only matters when choosing among more than one live opponent and this port's smart_target is already fixed to a single opponent at match creation; nor is calc_closest2's every-4th-tick recompute throttle, a pure CPU-cost optimization irrelevant to a fixed pair. closest_dist itself uses a standard integer square root rather than SQUARE.ASM's fast quantized table-lookup approximation, since near()/mode_block (the only real consumers) read only closest_xdist/closest_zdist, which are exact either way. Each of the 6 wired attacks' own leading ANI_SETFACING is now translated too (attack_sets_facing_on_start in src/core/bret_backend.c): 5 of the 6 (hrt_2/4_punch_anim, hrt_4_super_punch_anim, hrt_2_kick_anim, hrt_2/4_super_kick_anim) carry a real, instant FACING_DIR=NEW_FACING_DIR copy right at their own start, before any WL frame -- the same 'ANI_SETMODE is a zero-tick instant command' reasoning already used for MODE_UNINT/MODE_INTURN, gated on the animation actually (re)starting rather than firing on every call so it matches the source's real once-per-selection timing. hrt_4_kick_anim is confirmed (by reading its own header, not assumed from the other 5) to be the one real exception with no ANI_SETFACING at all. Wiring this also closed a small, separate, previously-flagged gap discovered while re-reading HRTSEQ2.ASM: hrt_4_super_kick_anim (HRTSEQ2.ASM:1334-1335) is a literal SUBR alias of hrt_2_super_kick_anim, same address, not distinct artwork, so WM_BRET_ANIM_SUPER_KICK4 now maps to the same real wm_bret_power_kick_anim data and hand-traced ATTACK_ON window SUPER_KICK2 already had, instead of staying unmapped. The leg turn anims' own ANI_XFLIP is now translated too (4 of the 6 canonical rotate_table bodies -- the two adjacent-quadrant ones, e.g. up-right<->right, never cross the sprite's own left/right mirror line and carry none): wm_bret_backend_tick toggles OBJ_CONTROL's M_FLIPH at its real, hand-traced frame index, the same mechanism already established for the torso's ANI_SETFACING. CAN_MOVE_DIR ring-boundary redirection is now real: wm/arcade/wm_arcade_confine.h's wm_arcade_confine_wrestler translates WRESTLE.ASM:3074 confine_wrestler's in-ring branch -- MODE_NOCONFINE/PLYRMODE==ATTACHED early-out, Z bounds against RING_TOP/RING_BOT, and X bounds against the real left/right rope boundary lines, reusing the already-translated wm/arcade/wmania_ring_geometry.h boundary seed data (fix38 Ring Chunk 1) via a new wm_ring_calc_line_x that computes WRESTLE.ASM:5814 calc_line_x's real per-Z interpolation directly (closed form of the source's own precomputed-table setup routine, including its genuine one-step inset quirk) instead of caching a table this port has no boot phase for. The X check reads actor->hurt_box.x1/x2 exactly where the source reads OBJ_COLLX1/OBJ_COLLX2 -- wm_arcade_set_hurt_box (already real) computes byte-identical values, since it's the same set_collision_boxes translation (COLLIS.ASM:260-354). Clamps x_int/z_int (and their _fixed twins) so the collision-box edge lands exactly on the boundary and sets the real WM_MOVE_* bits in the new actor->can_move_dir field, which wm/movement.h's wm_execute_walk now reads for the real down-right/down-left redirect (WRESTLE.ASM:5339-5384). Wired into wm_match_tick for the Bret actor only (the one actor with a real, moving position and hurt_box), right after its hurt_box is set fresh and before position integration. Not translated: the source actually runs confine_wrestler twice per tick and ORs the two CAN_MOVE_DIR results together (WRESTLE.ASM:3743-3752 confine_wrestler_fix1/fix2, whose own comment explains confine_wrestler happens twice per tick for whatever reason) -- that only converges because OBJ_COLLX1/2 get refreshed from the corrected position before the second call, and neither the second call site nor what refreshes the collision box in between is located in the checked-in source; a naive second pass reusing the same, now-stale hurt_box was tried and confirmed to diverge (double-applying nearly the same correction, overshooting past the boundary the other way) rather than converge, so only the genuine single real pass is kept. Also not translated, all for the same underlying reason -- this port's Bret actor never grapples/attaches (ATTACH_PROC) or leaves the ring (in_ring only ever starts and stays 1/true, no ring-out/knockback system clears it): ATTACH_PROC paired-actor movement and the rope-wobble bounce velocity/sound effects on first contact; ck_climb_out_top/bot/side (WRESTLE2.ASM, already translated as pure logic in wm/arcade/wmania_ring_climb.h via an earlier fix38 chunk but not wired to any real animation system, since triggering a climb is a presentation concern layered on top of the confinement computed here); the #outring branch entirely (ARENA_TOP/BOT, the fence lines, and the further mat2-edge climb-in overlap check that also touches CAN_MOVE_DIR) -- genuinely unreached while in_ring never leaves 1; and the PLYRMODE==RUNNING gate-crash tail (hit a gate, take damage, crash animation, zombie transform), which needs FACETBL/FACE24TBL animation-table dispatch this port hasn't translated on top of also being under the unreached #outring path. Also not translated: INIT_LADDER_TABLE/CURRENT_LADDER/NUM_OPPS multi-drone team selection (one placeholder opponent only, so #teamX_starts' second/third-player-on-team rows are never reached). DRONE.ASM's AI decision core and script interpreter (wm_arcade_drone_main/wm_arcade_drone_script_step) are now given real data and real callback bodies too: wm/arcade/wm_arcade_bret_drone.h supplies the blkbase_t/blkatk_t/sklhhdly_t/sklhrdly_t/sklrep_t skill tables (the SKLM macro that emits them turned out to be present in the checked-in source tree after all -- an earlier claim that it wasn't is corrected here), Bret's own real short/medium/long-range script lists (bret_s_t/bret_m_t/bret_l_t and everything they reference), and real callback implementations for every DS_CODE inline-native-code block the interpreter needed a way to run (drone_chkrun, drone_chrg, drn_run/drn_roll/drn_seek/drn_retreat/drn_climbtb-drn_ontb/drn_inair/drn_opinair/drn_oppdead, drone_seekdirdist's sine-table circling math) -- extending wm_arcade_drone_callbacks_t.script_call/script_seek to report the skip/abort/redirect outcomes those blocks' own addk 32,a9 / clr a9 / jump a1 tricks need, and fixing a real, previously-dormant bug where WM_DRONE_SC_DONE (DS_SLP1) cleared the script instead of yielding one tick. Since only Bret has a real move/animation backend in this port, the per-wrestler branches (range_script_list, drn_combo, drone_chrg) only hand out real attack content when the drone-controlled actor is itself Bret; the shared, wrestler-agnostic majority of the engine (positioning, block detection with real skill-scaled percentages, getup timing, run/roll/turnbuckle/in-air/dead-opponent handling) now runs for any wrestler pairing. wm_match_tick also now computes wm_arcade_calc_closest for every actor every tick, not just whichever one carries a real Bret backend, so a drone actor's own decisions read fresh distances instead of a tick-stale value. CHECK_COMBO_GO still always reports "not lit" in this port (wm_arcade_mode_dead.h's own prior finding), so drn_combo's button-mash combo-punch finisher is transcribed for completeness but, like the source's own empty combo meter, is never actually reachable. A CPU-controlled wrestler now genuinely presses buttons and pushes the stick -- a CPU-controlled Bret genuinely walks toward, blocks, and attacks. wm_arcade_move_bret's own MODE_DEAD dispatch now reaches a real wm_arcade_mode_dead (DOINK.ASM's shared mode_dead, referenced by every wrestler's own mode_table, including BRET.ASM's): in this port the real routine's royal_rumble/is_8_on_1/CHECK_COMBO_GO gates are all provably always false (no royal rumble mode, no 8-on-1 ladder battles, and no per-player combo-meter-fill tracking, since only life itself is real via init_life_data), so every branch collapses to the same outcome: WM_STATUS_NO_BUCKOFF gets set once on a wrestler's first dead tick and every following tick is a genuine no-op, exactly matching the source's own top-of-function early-outs. The button-mashing buckoff-revival system and the zombie-transform tail it leads to remain real but permanently unreachable while that stays true. A genuine death now also runs LIFEBAR.ASM's own death-dispatch tail (wm_arcade_adjust_health, wm/arcade/wm_arcade_lifebar.h): ROLL_POS resets, and the victim's own player_mode at the moment of death (NORMAL/RUNNING/INAIR/INAIR2/BOUNCING/ONTURNBKL/BLOCK/DIZZY/CLIMBTURNBKL -- every mode Bret's own real dispatcher can actually be in at death) selects the real fall_back anim (already wired as WM_BRET_ANIM_FALL_BACK) plus a real knockback velocity away from whoever landed the killing hit, wired through both real death paths (the REACT1.ASM hit path and BRET.ASM's own I_WILL_DIE self-death case) via a small death_anim callback bridge. The source's own ATTACK_MODE/DEAD_ANIM-bit pre-checks that skip the whole dispatch are translated too, though always false in this port today since none of Bret's wired attacks use those attack_mode ids. Not translated: death sound (this port's Bret backend leaves every other real sound call a no-op too, so adding one bridge just for this would be inconsistent), the #grnd convulse_t/hitonground dispatch and the #will_die HEADHELD deferral (both real but permanently unreachable since this port's Bret dispatcher never sets WM_PMODE_ONGROUND or WM_PMODE_HEADHELD), and flash_red (no lifebar rendering system exists here). Bret's secret moves (charge/neck-grab-style directional gestures) were real data since an earlier pass -- wm_arcade_bret_secret_patterns' 8 value/mask sequences and wm_arcade_bret_fire_secret's own per-move condition/dispatch logic -- but nothing ever detected the actual joystick sequence to call them with: wm_arcade_bret_callbacks_t.check_secret_moves was left unwired. wm/arcade/wm_arcade_joystat.h now translates WRESTLE.ASM's real update_joystat (the shared 16-entry-deep per-wrestler input-history ring buffer, including its facing-relative xflip_table remap and per-button insert loop) and check_secret_moves (the backward-walking value/mask matcher, including its own shared 8-entry skip budget for noise between real steps and its max_ticks timing window), wired into wm_bret_backend_callbacks for real. A human genuinely typing a sequence like down-down-punch now reaches wm_arcade_bret_fire_secret through real input, not just a direct call. Deliberately not translated: bret_secret_moves' own first entry, #charge_ddt, is executable hold-test code (not a value/mask table) gating a distinct charge-and-release move whose own underlying charge-duration timer (get_powerp_dtime) this port doesn't track yet -- a separate gap, not conflated with this recognizer, and wm_arcade_bret_secret_patterns' 8 entries already exclude it for exactly that reason. Also worth noting: none of the 8 secret moves' target animations have real extracted wm_visual_sequence frame data yet (only Bret's stand/torso/punch/kick basics do), so a fired secret move's anim selection is real and recorded (wm_bret_backend_actor.current_id) but currently gets no WM_MODE_UNINT protection and can be immediately reselected by the same tick's ordinary mode_normal continuation -- the identical, already-accepted limitation the FALL_BACK self-death path has. Chased down what was actually blocking that visual protection and fixed it properly instead of leaving it as an accepted gap. First, a real, confirmed pre-existing bug: WM_BRET_SECRET_SUPERCUT dispatched to a separate, permanently-unmapped WM_BRET_ANIM_SUPER_PUNCH4 id, when BRET.ASM's own #scrt_cut ("movi hrt_4_super_punch_anim,a0") selects the exact same real animation WM_BRET_ANIM_SUPER_PUNCH2_4 already maps to -- reusing that id (and removing the now-dead SUPER_PUNCH4) gives the super cut real frame data, its existing attack window, and real WM_MODE_UNINT/ANI_SETFACING protection for free, with zero new plumbing. Second, for the other 9 secret-move target ids that genuinely have no extracted frame data (JUMP_KICK4, RUNNING_DDT, HH_DDT2, HIPTOSS, GRABFLING_FACE24, RAKE_FACE, HEAD_HOLD2_3, HEAD_HOLD3, FAKE_HOLD3), read each one's own real HRTSEQ header directly and confirmed every one of them does lead with the same ANI_SETMODE,MODE_UNINT|MODE_NOAUTOFLIP as the 6 already-wired attacks (3 also carry the same instant ANI_SETFACING). wm_bret_backend_change_anim now applies that protection for these too, decoupled from requiring real frame data to detect a genuine new selection -- but since there is no wm_visual_state to time a real end from, wm_bret_backend_tick clears it back off the same tick it was set, a deliberate, bounded simplification (one tick of real protection, not the source's full per-animation duration) rather than either leaving the original silent-overwrite bug in place or risking a permanent WM_MODE_UNINT soft-lock by guessing at timing this port doesn't have. Also translated three more real, previously-dormant BRET.ASM mechanisms this unlocked. First, WRESTLE.ASM's own update_joy_dtime (#update_but half): a real per-button hold-duration counter (wm_arcade_update_joy_dtime, wm/arcade/wm_arcade_combat.h), reset to 0 the instant a button is released, matching punch_dtime1/powerp_dtime1/powerk_dtime1's own BSS layout. Second, bret_secret_moves' own real first entry, #charge_ddt (executable hold-test code, not a value/mask table -- previously excluded from the recognizer as a separate, not-yet-tracked gap): now checked every tick via wm_arcade_bret_try_charge_ddt, using that real dtime, taking priority over the pattern scan exactly like the source's own early return. Third, two more independent persistent-process watchers with the identical hold-then-release shape, hrt_charge_flying_kick/hrt_charge_face_rake (BRET.ASM:543/614) -- wm_arcade_bret_release_charge_flying_kick/release_charge_face_rake already had real condition/dispatch logic, just never a caller. Both defer their fired animation through the real SPECIAL_MOVE_ADDR handoff (WRESTLE.ASM:3843-3849 move_wrestler: "if a special move watchdog proc has queued up an anim, do that instead of calling move_xxx") rather than calling change_anim1a directly like #charge_ddt does, since they run as genuinely separate CREATEd processes in the source rather than synchronously inside the wrestler's own move_bret call -- wm_arcade_move_bret now consumes that handoff for real too, the one piece that let any of wm_arcade_bret_fire_monitor's own real dispatch logic (headhold moves, roll uppercut, grab-toss-air, the finishers) ever have visible effect, though none of those are reachable yet without their own real trigger (a persistent input-monitor scheduler this port doesn't have, or -- for the headhold moves -- the headhold grapple state this port's Bret dispatcher never enters). Not translated in this pass and stated rather than papered over: ANI_WAITROLL (171 uses) needs the roll/getup system behind it (do_roll, I_WILL_DIE, GETUP_TIME, clear_lifebar), and ANI_WAITHITGND2 (ANIM.ASM:4043) has no uses at all across the eight playable wrestlers. A knocked-down wrestler can get up now, and the whole loop is real. ANI_WAITROLL (ANIM.ASM:2990, 171 uses) parks the animation, forces MODE_ONGROUND ("just to be safe", the source says), waits out IMMOBILIZE_TIME and GETUP_TIME, then calls WRESTLE2.ASM:1290 do_roll -- and it is do_roll answering "did NOT roll" that lets the animation move on, so letting go of the stick is what gets him up. hrt_tossed_anim therefore runs end to end: thrown and launched, ANI_WAITHITGND for the landing, ANI_GETUP,STAY_TIME's 270 ticks down on the mat, the roll, then ANI_CHANGEANIM,hrt_faceup_getup_anim. do_roll's eight per-wrestler tables are extracted by tools/wlroll.py into src/generated/roll_frames.c: a speed, a Z velocity and an inverse multiplier followed by a frame list, with an 8-bit ROLL_POS run through the multiplier to pick the frame. The lists are not in ascending order -- Bret's runs FR1 then FR13 down to FR2, the direction his artwork rolls -- and holding up rather than down negates both the advance and the Z velocity so the frames run the other way too; Z_BOUND stops him once he is within 6 of it. One source detail preserved rather than tidied: the multipliers are written as expressions like 10000h*12/255 and the assembler's divide truncates, so Bret's is 3084, the largest index a 0..255 ROLL_POS can reach is 11, and his thirteenth frame is unreachable in the shipped game. WRESTLE.ASM:2538's getup meter is what makes it playable: GETUP_TIME counts down one a tick and any button or stick press -- or its release edge, via STATUS_FLAGS' M_PRESS_LAST -- takes three more off, which turns a 270-tick stay-down into about 69 ticks of mashing; reaching zero clears PLYR_DIZZY and STARS_FLAG. ANI_GETUP (:52) sets it and refuses while PLYR_DIZZY is set. This also closes a loop wm/arcade/wm_arcade_lifebar.h had flagged in its own notes: adjust_health's #will_die path defers a death by setting i_will_die rather than killing outright, and the header recorded that it "needs an eventual consumer this port doesn't have" -- ANI_WAITROLL is that consumer, and calls clear_lifebar (LIFEBAR.ASM:5310, life half only; update_meter is pure rendering) when the debt comes due. ANI_ROT (:4441) came with it: "just sit and do nothing", holding the current frame and never advancing, which is how xxx_dead_anim keeps a dead wrestler down. It is a terminator for span purposes even though it is not an ANI_END, which is what lets xxx_dead_anim be emitted at all -- four commands and a rot, with no frames -- and it had to be, because ANI_WAITROLL hands off to it. 519 programs; 88.3% of every ANI_* across the eight playable wrestlers. NOT translated and unreachable in this port's match mode rather than skipped: _ani_waitroll's #dead drone branches (is_8_on_1, royal_rumble, FINAL_PTR's zombie promotion, adjust_health) -- in an ordinary match a player takes jreq #die immediately and a drone reaches the same jruc #die with is_8_on_1 false and royal_rumble zero, so both land on the hand-off that is translated; the getup meter's match_time expiry (this port has no round-timer countdown); and its two .if DEBUG stay_down branches, which are not in the shipped build. Finally, a defect shipped in the gravity change was found and fixed here: wlprogram's MOTION_OPS, the set deciding which ops get their operands written into the generated C, was a hand-kept list, so an op added to the command table but not to that set fell through to the no-operand default and had its operands silently emitted as zero. ANI_BOUNCE's upward kick became 0 and ANI_GETUP's stay time became 0. Neither test caught it -- the bounce test checked the extractor's tuple rather than the emitted C, and the fall test passed on the first launch, which comes from a different opcode. The set is derived from the command table now, and a test checks both the derivation and the two real values in the generated file.
